eligible.content: I think I'll stick with the schedule for now and focus on the check-ins. But maybe we can go over the signs of needing water during one of the sessions? I don't want to guess wrong and overwater or underwater.

That's a very wise way to approach it. Focusing on those specific signs is much safer than guessing! When you're checking your plants, what are the most common "signs" you're looking for—like leaf wilting, yellowing, or soil dryness? Knowing what those specific indicators are will help us keep the watering spot-on!

sources.content: I think a general schedule would be easier to start with. Maybe something like checking each pot every two hours during the hottest part of the day? Does that sound reasonable?

That sounds like a solid, proactive approach! Checking every two hours during the peak heat of the day is definitely smart; it ensures you don't miss anything important while the sun is strongest. Do you want to track specific types of plants separately in that schedule, or are we looking for one general "check-in" time for the whole group?

I see what you mean about different plants having different needs. Maybe I can start with a daily check-in at noon and another in the late afternoon? That way I'm covering the main heat hours without overdoing it. Does that work for you?

That sounds like a very practical approach! Dividing the day into those two check-in points—one at noon and another in the late afternoon—seems like a great way to manage the high heat without exhausting yourself.
